author: Recorded by the Brothers of the Lantern

#An Account of the Long Freeze

In the eleventh year of the reign of Jarl Torvald the Lame, the snow came early and did not leave. This account was gathered from the testimony of survivors and set down by our order so that the lesson would not be lost.

#The First Signs

The autumn harvest was poor but not alarming. The rivers froze a month before the usual time, and the old women said the geese had flown south in silence, which they took as a bad omen. Nobody listened to the old women. Nobody ever does.

By midwinter the snow had buried the lowland farms to their rooftops. Families dug tunnels from house to house and burned their furniture, then their fences, then their doors.

#Spring That Did Not Come

When the month of planting arrived, the snow was still deeper than a man is tall. The sun rose pale and small, and gave no warmth. Some said a dragon had cursed the land. Others blamed the jarl, the elves, the Daedra or the moons, according to taste.

What is certain is that the granaries emptied. The jarl opened his own stores to the people, which is to his credit, but his stores were not enough. Many of the old and very young did not live to see green grass again.

#The Long Hunt

The hold survived because of its hunters. Bands of men and women on snowshoes went out for weeks at a time, following herds of elk into valleys no one had mapped. They brought back meat, hides and stories of strange things seen in the white silence: lights moving under the ice, and a great shape that passed overhead one night and blotted out the stars.

When the thaw finally came, in the second summer, the hunters were honoured above the jarl's own guard. Their descendants still wear a strip of white fur on their collars.

#The Lesson

Our order keeps a lantern burning in every village we serve, as a promise that no winter lasts forever. We also keep careful records of every harvest, and we nag every jarl to fill the granaries in good years.

They find us tiresome. We find this acceptable.
